title: Fetch all
hints: Work in three phases, and only the middle one is concurrent: (1) in the caller, de-duplicate `keys` into a `unique` slice (first occurrence wins); (2) one goroutine per unique key writes a small `result{value, err}` into `results[i]`; (3) after `Wait`, build the maps and `Failed` from `unique` and `results`.

Put the fetch in a helper `fetchOne(f, key) (res result)` with a deferred `recover` that sets the named result, so a panic becomes `fmt.Errorf("fetch %q panicked: %v", key, r)`. A normal error becomes `fmt.Errorf("fetch %q: %w", key, err)`. Handle `""` before starting a goroutine: `results[i].err = ErrEmptyKey`.

Phase 3: `rep := Report{Values: make(map[string]string), Errors: make(map[string]error), Failed: []string{}}`, then `for i, key := range unique { if results[i].err != nil { rep.Errors[key] = results[i].err; rep.Failed = append(rep.Failed, key) } else { rep.Values[key] = results[i].value } }` and `slices.Sort(rep.Failed)`. The `seen` map in phase 1 is fine: only the calling goroutine touches it.
